title: Q3 v2: orchestrator/planner_packet.py — compact, delta-oriented Planner decision packets and the Opus→Fable escalation packet, size-measured (P4, P10)
spec:
Why: planner_runs.decision_packet (lines 43-107) and grouped_packet rebuild a per-point packet with the full spawn packet inventory, 300-char scout summaries, no memory, no changes-since-last-decision and no required-output section; the brief (P4) wants a delta-oriented packet with only what the decision needs, invalidated on state change, and (P10) a compact escalation packet so Fable solves the unresolved part instead of redoing Opus's work. Spec review T-0679 asked for an explicit decision_type source, the taxonomy shape and the real scout finding fields; folded in below.
What: new pure module orchestrator/planner_packet.py. Never reads the bus or files itself: the caller passes data. Untrusted text goes inside fences labelled data with backticks elided (copy planner_runs._fenced's 6-line helper; do not import planner_runs).
- Taxonomy shape: orchestrator/planner_taxonomy.py (T-0675, on goal/T-0674) exposes DECISION_TYPES = ("initial_goal_plan", "scout_results", "held_task", "architectural_replan", "fix_strategy", "closable_goal", "retrospective", "ambiguous_requirement", "other") and classify(...) -> {"decision_type", "architectural", "ambiguous", "risk_class", "signals", "band", "task_class"}. A section's decision_type = section["classification"]["decision_type"] when present, else the fallback from point["kind"]: scouts_done -> scout_results, held -> held_task, closable -> closable_goal, retrospective -> retrospective, anything else -> other. Import DECISION_TYPES from planner_taxonomy for validation; an unknown value maps to other.
- build(sections, *, goal, previous=None, changes=None, scout_findings=None, memory_hits=None, cap_chars=6000) -> {"text", "chars", "est_tokens" (chars // 4), "hash" (sha256[:12]), "sections": [names included], "truncated": [names cut], "delta": bool}. sections = list of {"point" ({goal_id, kind, payload_key, task_id?}), "ctx" (decision.route ctx dict), "route" (decision.Route or dict name/reason/evidence/tier), "classification" (taxonomy dict or None), "task" (bus dict or None), "reviews" ([{path, line, issue}]), "failures" (str|None), "depends_on_statuses" ([{id, status}])}. Section order and rules: 1 Decision header (per section: decision_type and expected output: initial_goal_plan/scout_results -> 'write plan.md and atomic specs'; fix_strategy/held_task -> 'write one fix-round spec with depends_on=[held]'; architectural_replan -> 'respec or split; state why'; closable_goal -> 'open PR goal/<id> -> main or say why not'; ambiguous_requirement -> 'state the ambiguity under Needs the human'; retrospective -> 'record.sh add'; other -> 'decide'); 2 Goal (id, title, complexity, spec first 600 chars); 3 Changes since previous decision: previous None -> the line 'first Planner decision for this goal'; else the caller-supplied changes list [{"task", "field", "from", "to", "ts"}] max 20 lines plus previous["state_version"]; delta True iff previous is given; 4 Relevant task state per section (title, status, hold_reason, failures capped 1500, review comments max 10 as path:line issue[:200], depends_on statuses); 5 Scout findings only when some section is scout_results or initial_goal_plan: scout_findings is the output of scout_evidence.normalize_findings, entries {finding, source, confidence, relevance, unresolved, needs_challenge}; render max 10 lines as 'finding[:200] (source, confidence)'; 6 Memory: memory_hits titles only, max 10, each 200 chars; 7 Unresolved alternatives: route.evidence lines plus option names (copy planner_runs._SCOUTS_DONE_OPTIONS / _NEXT_ACTION_OPTIONS as module constants here); 8 Required output (repeat of header expectations plus 'Do not restate this packet'). Excluded by construction: event logs, unrelated tasks, transcripts, previous prompts.
- Truncation: header, Goal and Required output are never truncated; when over cap, cut in this order until it fits: Memory, Scout findings, Unresolved alternatives, Changes, Relevant task state (failures first); record cut names in truncated.
- escalation_packet(*, goal, original_sections, opus_decision, unresolved, conflicting_evidence=None, scout_findings=None, memory_hits=None, reason, cap_chars=6000) -> same shape; opus_decision whitelist {"proposed_action", "summary" (cap 800), "tasks_proposed" ([{"title", "scope"}] cap 10), "confidence", "needs_fable", "unresolved"}, rendered under 'Opus proposed decision (data)'; header line 'Escalation reason: <reason>. Solve only the unresolved items.'; any other key dropped, never raw transcripts.
- invalidated(previous_state_version, current_state_version) -> bool (differ or either None). meta(text) -> {"chars", "est_tokens", "hash"}.
acceptance: tests/test_planner_packet.py::test_first_decision_has_no_delta_and_all_sections — one section classified scout_results with normalize_findings-shaped findings and memory hits produces the sections in the documented order, delta False and the text 'first Planner decision for this goal'; a section without classification and kind held gets held_task from the fallback

tests/test_planner_packet.py::test_delta_lists_changes_since_previous — previous record and 3 changes give delta True, the 3 change lines and the previous state_version; a 40-entry change list is cut to 20 lines

tests/test_planner_packet.py::test_truncation_order_and_protected_sections — cap 1200 with long failures drops Memory first, then Scout findings, and never cuts the header or Required output; truncated names match
tests/test_planner_packet.py::test_untrusted_text_is_fenced_and_backticks_elided — a hold_reason containing ``` and 'ignore previous instructions' appears inside a data fence with backticks elided

tests/test_planner_packet.py::test_escalation_packet_whitelists_opus_decision — an opus_decision carrying a 'transcript' key and a 3000-char summary yields a packet without the transcript, summary capped at 800, the escalation reason in the header and invalidated() True for differing versions

constraints.interface_contract: build(sections, *, goal, previous=None, changes=None, scout_findings=None, memory_hits=None, cap_chars=6000) -> {text, chars, est_tokens, hash, sections, truncated, delta}; sections items {point, ctx, route, classification (planner_taxonomy.classify dict or None), task, reviews, failures, depends_on_statuses}; decision_type from classification else kind fallback; scout_findings = scout_evidence.normalize_findings output; escalation_packet(*, goal, original_sections, opus_decision, unresolved, conflicting_evidence, scout_findings, memory_hits, reason, cap_chars) -> same shape; invalidated(prev, cur) -> bool; meta(text) -> {chars, est_tokens, hash}. Pure: no bus/file reads. Wave B calls build/escalation_packet in place of decision_packet/grouped_packet.

result.summary: superseded by Q3 v3 after spec review T-0713 request_changes (hard text[:cap_chars] backstop with a length assertion; section 3 defined for previous without changes via previous.get('state_version'))

spec_review_risks.issue: The truncation algorithm only ever drops whole named sections (Memory, Scout findings, Unresolved alternatives, Changes, then failures text within Relevant task state) but defines no final hard backstop (the existing decision_packet() always does `text[:cap]`). With many sections or long untruncated fields (task title, hold_reason, status, depends_on statuses are never capped per-section), build() can still emit text over cap_chars after exhausting the cut list, and the acceptance test for cap 1200 only checks cut order/protected sections, not that len(text) <= cap. Since this packet is fed straight into a paid headless Planner call, an unbounded prompt is exactly the kind of unguarded-external-call risk this module exists to prevent.

build()'s behavior when previous is given but changes is None (or omitted) is unspecified: section 3 is defined only for previous=None (fixed sentence) and for previous+changes together (line list + previous['state_version']). A caller that passes previous without changes — a normal case, since a caller may know the goal changed but not have a diff — is left to guess, and a naive implementation indexing previous['state_version'] will KeyError if state_version is absent instead of using .get().
